name: Chicken and vegetable noodle stir-fry
summary: Wholewheat noodles tossed in a hot wok with chicken strips, baby corn, sugar snap peas, pak choi, cabbage and red pepper in a garlic, ginger, soy and lime sauce.
about: Stir-fried noodles are cooked across China and South-East Asia: the noodles are boiled first, then tossed over high heat with meat, vegetables and a little sauce so they stay springy. Sharpened with lime rather than a sweet glaze, this version needs one pot and one wok on a school night.

ingredients.name: Limes
ingredients.note: 1 juiced for the sauce, 1 cut into wedges to serve

ingredients.name: Pak choi
ingredients.note: about 3 heads, stems sliced, leaves kept apart

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat. Drop in the noodles and cook for the time on the packet, usually 4 to 5 minutes, until soft with a little bite left. Drain, rinse under the cold tap so they stop cooking, then toss with 1 tsp of the oil so the strands stay separate.
While the water heats, mix the soy sauce, the juice of one lime, the 4 tbsp water and the cornflour in a jug until the cornflour has dissolved.

Set a wok or your largest frying pan over high heat with 1 tbsp of the oil. When it shimmers, spread the chicken out in the pan, let it sit for 1 minute to colour, then keep it moving for another 3 minutes, until golden with no pink left inside the thickest strip. Move it to a plate.

Pour in the last of the oil and add the baby corn, sugar snaps, red pepper and pak choi stems. Keep tossing over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the corn and peas are bright and the pepper is just beginning to soften.
Add the cabbage, pak choi leaves, garlic and ginger and toss for 1 to 2 minutes more, until the leaves have wilted and the garlic smells fragrant without browning.

Tip the chicken and noodles back in. Stir the sauce once more, pour it over and turn everything with tongs for 1 to 2 minutes, until the noodles are hot and evenly coated and no sauce is left pooling in the pan.
Pile into bowls, scatter with the spring onions and coriander and serve with the lime wedges for squeezing.
prepNote: Slice the chicken and vegetables and mix the sauce up to a day ahead; keep them covered in the fridge.
